citation: Brookshire, Kasper, Blauch, et al. (2024). Frontiers in Neuroscience, 18, 1373515
datasets: Private AD/SCI EEG (Pacific Neuroscience Institute; Ganapathi et al., 2022); Siena Scalp EEG (seizures)
models: Reproduced 1D-CNN (Oh et al., 2020) and frequency-domain DNN (Rashed-Al-Mahfuz et al., 2021)
validation: segment-based holdout vs subject-based holdout on identical models
main_claim: Segment-based holdout leaks subject identity and strongly overestimates performance on unseen subjects; most translational DNN-EEG studies use it.
key_numbers: Only 17/63 (27.0%) surveyed studies unambiguously avoided subject leakage
methods_terms: subject-based vs segment-based holdout; identity confounding; reproduction of published architectures; systematic survey of split strategy
limitations: Two datasets; DNNs only; leakage type limited to subject identity
gap_for_us: Does not address demographic or cohort/acquisition confounds, foundation models, or cross-cohort testing

citation: Miltiadous, Ntetska, Aspiotis, et al. (2026). Cognitive Neurodynamics, 20(1)
validation: studies stratified into validity tiers: 1 subject-level CV (e.g. LOSO), 2 subject-level split, 3 epoch-level k-fold
main_claim: Methodological rigour is inversely related to reported accuracy on AHEPA; data leakage drives apparent gains of deep models.
key_numbers: AD vs CN mean accuracy 90.81% overall vs 82.11% in Validity-1; FTD vs CN 86.53% vs 75.18%; weaker validation adds 7-10 pp
methods_terms: validity-tier stratification; normalisation of metrics across classification problems; linear regression of accuracy on validation rigour; PRISMA
limitations: Single dataset; accuracy as the main metric
gap_for_us: Explicitly notes lack of cross-configuration generalisation and need for montage-independent methods; we test cross-cohort transfer and acquisition confounds

citation: Lin, Wu, Jung, et al. (2026). arXiv:2606.06647
datasets: 4 public resting-state datasets incl. Alzheimer's/FTD, mental arithmetic, sleep deprivation, trait stress (N<=65 each); 200 Hz, 1-45 Hz
models: Frozen and fine-tuned LaBraM, CBraMod, REVE
validation: subject-disjoint CV; a priori 2x2 design (label within/between subject x consensus marker present)
main_claim: Subject identity dominates frozen EEG-FM representations (the 'Identity Trap'); it lies on a largely linear, removable axis; aperiodic 1/f is one carrier for LaBraM/CBraMod.
key_numbers: Subject-variance fraction 13-89x a random-Gaussian null in 12/12 pairs; erasure improves within-subject label decoding by +6 to +12 pp; removing aperiodic 1/f drops subject probe 9-19 pp (LaBraM, CBraMod)
methods_terms: FMScope pre-flight protocol; variance decomposition; subject-axis erasure with LEACE; aperiodic 1/f ablation; layer-wise label probing; within-subject direction consistency
limitations: Small datasets; within-cohort; subject identity rather than demographics/site
gap_for_us: Does not test cohort/acquisition identity or demographics, nor cross-cohort generalisation after erasure (our O2-O4)
